title: Finite cohomology below a pseudo-coherent bound
statement: Let R be a commutative ring with identity (including the zero ring, as in the Stacks conventions) and m an integer. Let D(R) be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of R-modules. Call an object C of D(R) m-pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent] if there are a bounded complex E^\bullet of finite free R-modules and a morphism E^\bullet\to C in D(R) inducing isomorphisms H^i(E^\bullet)\to H^i(C) for i>m and a surjection H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C). If K^\bullet is a complex of R-modules, viewed as an object of D(R), which is m-pseudo-coherent and satisfies H^i(K^\bullet)=0 for every i>m, then H^m(K^\bullet) is a finite type R-module.

proof.text: Choose a bounded finite-free witness E^\bullet\to K^\bullet for the m-pseudo-coherence hypothesis; finite free modules are finite projective, so E^\bullet is a bounded complex of finite projective R-modules. Because H^i(K^\bullet)=0 for i>m and the witness induces isomorphisms in those degrees, H^i(E^\bullet)=0 for every i>m.

Working with finite projective modules (the splitting below need not preserve freeness): if the largest degree b with E^b\ne0 satisfies b>m, then H^b(E^\bullet)=0 makes d^{b-1}:E^{b-1}\to E^b surjective. Since E^b is finite projective, split this surjection and write E^{b-1}=E'^{b-1}\oplus E^b so that the differential on the second summand is the identity. Removing the resulting contractible two-term summand leaves a bounded complex of finite projectives with the same cohomology and top degree at most b-1. Repeating finitely many times gives E'^\bullet with E'^i=0 for i>m and H^m(E')\cong H^m(E^\bullet). Then H^m(E')=E'^m/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1}) is a quotient of the finitely generated module E'^m, hence finite type.
The witness map induces a surjection H^m(E^\bullet)\twoheadrightarrow H^m(K) by m-pseudo-coherence. A quotient of a finite type module is finite type, so H^m(K) is finite type.
